questions.question: What is the income of all the residents of the country called?
questions.solution: Total income is the sum of the incomes of people who form the workforce of the country. However, per capita income or average income is the total income of the country divided by number of people in that country.

questions.question: Under which article the President declares 'Presidents Rule' in India?
questions.solution:
Option **2** is correct, i.e. __**Article 356**__.

__
 
• Article 356__ of the Constitution gives the President the right to use it only where he is satisfied that a situation has arisen where the government of that state cannot be run in accordance with the provisions of the Constitution.
 
• President can declare a national emergency on three grounds: War, External aggression, armed rebellion.
 __
 
• National Emergency - Article 352
 
• State Emergency - Article 356
 
• Financial Emergency - Article 360
 
 

**Extra facts:**

 
 

 Article__
 __Detail__
 
 

 Article 350
 Talks about the Language to be used in representation for redress of grievances.
 
 

 Article 352
 
 It can be proclaimed only when the security of India or a part of it is threatened by war, external aggression or armed rebellion
 
 
 

 Article 356
 It can be proclaimed when the government of a state cannot be carried on in accordance with the provisions of the Constitution due to reasons which may not have any connection with war, external aggression or armed rebellion
 
 

 Article 360
 The president can proclaim a financial emergency if he is satisfied that a situation has arisen due to which the financial stability or credit of India or any part of its territory is threatened.

questions.question: In which form of government, each adult citizen must have one vote and each vote must have one value?
questions.solution: One of the major features of the democracy is the Universal Adult Franchise wherein every adult citizen has one vote and each vote counts as one which can be casted by the person whose vote it is and by no one else.

questions.question: Where was the first capital of Chalukyas?
questions.solution: The First capital of Chalukya Dynasty was Aihole which is clear from the inscriptions found in the caves of Aihole. Later the capital was changed to Badami by Pulkeshin 1 in 543.

questions.question: Who raised the slogan "Swaraj is my birth right and I shall have it"?
questions.solution: Bal Gangadhar Tilak coined the phrase in Marathi emphasising the need of the nation for complete independence. The Indian National Congress recognised the need for Purna Swaraj and passed a resolution in 1929 declaring total independence.

questions.question: Why Earth is called the blue planet?

options.text: Because of two-thirds surface covered by water
Because of water laden clouds in the atmosphere
Because of pollution in the atmosphere

questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 1 i.e__** Because of the two-thirds surface covered by water**__

__
 
• Earth is called a blue planet because almost 66% of the surface is covered with water this makes it appear blue from outer space. Earth is the only planet known which has the existence of water in it.

 

 
• About 71% of the Earth’s surface is covered with water, which appears blue from space. And also, due to the atmosphere, the land appears quite hazy, which from a distance looks predominantly blue.
 
• Earth:
 
 
• The Earth is 23 ½ degrees tilted on its axis and thus makes 66 ½ degrees angle.
 
• It is known as a watery planet or blue planet due to the presence of huge amounts of water in it.
 
• Earth is the only known planet that provides sustenance or life on it.
 
• The mass of the Earth is 6×1024 kg and the mass of the Moon is 7× 1022 kg. 
 
 
 
• Jupiter__:
 
 
• Jupiter is the planet, orange in color with white bands on it.
 
• Jupiter is the largest planet in the Solar System.
 
• It is also known as the winter planet as its average temperature is very low.
 
• Jupiter's atmosphere is mostly made up of hydrogen (H₂) and helium (He).
 
• Ganymede, a satellite of Jupiter is the largest satellite in the solar system.
 
 
 
• Mars:
 
 
• Mars is reddish in color.
 
• Mars is also known as the Red Planet
 
• It is red in color due to the presence of iron oxides.
 
• Mars has two moons named Phobos and Deimos.
 
 
 
• Saturn:
 
 
• Saturn is known most for its rings.
 
• It is the second-largest planet in our solar system.
 
• Saturn's atmosphere is also mostly made up of hydrogen (H2) and helium (He).
 
• Titan is the largest satellite of Saturn

questions.question: What is the shape of the Pacific Ocean?
questions.solution: The Pacific Ocean covers about one-third of the earth's surface. Its shape is roughly triangular with its apex in the north at the Bering Strait.

questions.question: Heat is which component of habitat?
questions.solution: *Abiotic* or non-living things contribute to the physical components of the environment and are continually subjected in different situations in the physical environment such as erosion, typhoons, volcanic events, ocean current and etc. Some examples are water, soil, air, *heat* and light

questions.question: Pepsin digests ______.
questions.solution: Pepsin is an enzyme that breaks down proteins into smaller peptides (that is, a protease). It is produced in the stomach and is one of the main digestive enzymes in the digestive systems of humans.

questions.question: How many terminals does an electric cell has?
questions.solution: All electric cells have two terminals; a positive terminal and a negative terminal. The metal cap is the positive terminal of the electric cell and the metal disc is the negative terminal.

questions.question: The size of the image formed by a plane mirror is always _____ to/than the object.
questions.solution: The magnification of a plane mirror is always 1 and it forms images which are always of the same size as the object. This because the linear magnification produced by a mirror is equal to the ratio of the image distance to the object distance, with a minus sign.

questions.question: Microsoft excel is also called ______.
questions.solution: Microsoft Excel is application software that allows the user to make spreadsheets using various rows and columns to organise a particular set of information.

questions.question: ________ the correct formula for ammonium phosphate.
questions.solution: Ammonium phosphate is the salt of ammonium and phosphate. It is highly unstable. Its formula is (NH₄)₃PO₄. Because of its instability, it has no commercial value.

questions.question: Law of Triad was proposed by ________.
questions.solution: The law of triads was one of the first attempts to organise the elements when there was no periodic table. As per this law if you put the elements with similar physical properties in order of their atomic masses, the average of the molar mass of the first and third elements in a triad is the molar mass of the second element.

questions.question: What are the microorganisms that breakdown the dead remains and waste product of organisms called?
questions.solution:
• When plants and animals die, they become food for decomposers like bacteria, fungi and earthworms.
 
• Decomposers or saprotrophs recycle dead plants and animals into chemical nutrients like carbon and nitrogen that are released back into the soil, air and water.

questions.question: What is the rate of KrishiKalyan Cess which was proposed in budget 2016?
questions.solution: Unlike taxes, amounts collected via cess are meant be segregated in government accounts and used for a specific purpose. So KKC is to be solely used towards financing activities for the improvement of agriculture and farmer welfare. It came into effect from June 1, 2016.

questions.question: "Hitting below the belt" is a phrase associated with which sports?
questions.solution: The phrase ‘Hitting below the belt’ as used in the English language has been taken from the rule of not hitting the opponent below the belt level in boxing. As used in English it means an ‘unfair move’.

questions.question: The Vedas, Upanishads, Puranas and Dharmasutras are all written in which language?
questions.solution: The most ancient documents like Vedas, Upanishads, Puranas, and Dharmasutras are written in the Sanskrit language.

questions.question: Which airport in India is ranked first in customer satisfaction Index Survey conducted for the period of Jan-June 2017?
questions.solution: The award was announced by the Airports Council International (ACI), which represented 1,953 member airports in 176 countries.The selection of the Mumbai Airport was made on the basis of a worldwide programme in which passengers were surveyed across airports for their feedback on 34 key performance indicators.

questions.question: Where was the first International Agrobiodiversity Congress held?
questions.solution: The first International Agrobiodiversity Congress happened in New Delhi from 6-9 November, 2016 and saw a participation of 900 delegates from 60 countries. The discussion revolved around sustainable agricultural development.

questions.question: Petrapole Integrated Check Post is the South Asia's biggest land port that exists between India and ______.
questions.solution: Petrapole is the border checkpoint between India and Bangladesh, near Bongaon in North 24 Parganas district of West Bengal. Petrapole border is the only land port in south Bengal and is also the largest land customs station in Asia.
